Author: K. Sreenivasa Reddy
Bench: K. Sreenivasa Reddy
The Honourable Sri Justice K. Sreenivasa Reddy
 Criminal Petition No.15122 Of 2016
Order:

-
This Criminal Petition is filed to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.128 of 2010 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Banganapalli, Kurnool District.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Banganapalli, Kurnool District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard counsel for the petitioners and the Special Assistant Public Prosecutor for the State.
3.

The only ground that has been raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is that the opportunity to avail valuable right of the petitioners to send the sample for second analysis to the Central Food Laboratory after receipt of notice under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, 'the Act, 1954'), has been defeated by delaying the process of issuance of the said notice.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that on 26.08.2009 one sample was sent to Public analyst along with Form IV.
On analysis, the Public Analyst, vide report dated 06.10.2009, opined that the sample does not conform to the standard of melting point and hence, it is adulterated.
It is submitted that the a notice under Section 13 (2) of the Act, 1954 was sent to the petitioners, which was received by them on 02.06.2010, by which time the shelf life of the sample expired.

However, the petitioners, on receiving notice under Section 13(2) of the Act, 1954, made an application before the Court to send the second sample for analysis and the learned Magistrate ordered to send the second sample for reanalysis, but the prosecution failed to produce the sample stating that the sample is not traceable.
In view of the same, the petitioners could not avail the opportunity of sending the sample for reanalysis to the Central Food Laboratory.

4. Learned Special Assistant Public Prosecutor also concurred with the fact that the sample was not sent to the Central Food Laboratory and the petitioners could not avail the opportunity of getting sample tested before the Central Food Laboratory and the notice has been served on them at a belated stage.

5. In Narayana Prasad Sahu v. State of Madhya Pradesh1, the Apex Court held as follows:
"Under sub-section (2) of Section 13, it is mandatory for the Local (Health) Authority to forward a copy of the report of the Public Analyst to the person from whom the CRLP/15122/2016 on 9 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111238632/
1 sample of the food has been taken in such a manner as may be prescribed.

entities.text: Narayana Prasad Sahu v. State of Madhya Pradesh1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further mandate of sub-section (2) of Section 13 is that a person to whom the (2022) 1 Supreme Court Cases 87 report is forwarded should be informed that if it is so desired, he can make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample analysed by the Central Food Laboratory.
The report is required to be forwarded after institution of prosecution against the person from whom the sample of the article of food was taken.

Apart from the right of the accused to contend that the report is not correct, he has right to exercise an option of sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis by making an application to the court within ten days from the date of receipt of the report.

If a copy of the report of the Public Analyst is not delivered to the accused, his right under sub- section (2) of Section 13 of praying for sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory will be defeated.
Consequently, his right to challenge the report will be defeated.
His right to defend himself will be adversely affected.

This Court in Vijendra {(2020) 15 SCC 763}, held that mere dispatch of the report to the accused is not a sufficient compliance with the requirement of sub-section (2) of Section 13 and the report must be served on the accused."
6. Right conferred on the petitioners to send the sample to the Central Food Laboratory is not an empty formality.

The Apex Court consistently has stated that in case, if the petitioners are deprived of availing the opportunity of sending the sample to Central Food Laboratory, then, it is a case where the Court can interfere under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
In such case, continuation of the proceedings as against the petitioners is nothing but abuse of process of the Court.
7. In view of the same, the Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings in C.C.No.128 of 2010 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Banganapalli, Kurnool District, are quashed.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate, Banganapalli, Kurnool District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Criminal Petition, shall stand closed.
_ _ JUSTICE K. SREENIVASA REDDY 09.03.2022.
